newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares hit 25-mth lows as KL market dips.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares hit 25-mth lows as KL market dips.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) hit a 25-month low of 2,027.11 points on Tuesday afternoon, dragged lower by foreign fund selling and a drop in the neighbouring Malaysian stock market.
By 0810 GMT, the STII had recovered back to 2,031.31 points.
The last time the 30-share index was at an intraday level of 2,027 points was on February 27, 1995.
Dealers said the index looked poised for further falls.
"If it stays down here, I think the chartists will push it down. Technical support has already been broken and people are talking about 1,900 if support at 2,000 goes," said a dealer.
Dealers said some of the selling in the wider market was in Malaysian shares traded over-the-counter in Singapore.
Pressure for liquidation of these stocks came from Kuala Lumpur where the Composite Index reached an eight-month low of 1,080.83 points, down 20.26, before recovering slightly.
But they said the Singapore market was expected to hold up better than the Malaysian stock market, which has fallen by 15 percent over the last couple of months.
"We're not expecting a meltdown," said another dealer. "There's not a lot to worry about in Singapore and foreign holdings here are not very heavy."
Shares in state shipping company Neptune Orient Lines, which resumed trading on Tuesday after announcing a takeover bid for U.S.-based carrier APL, were last up five cents at S$1.25.
Dealers said the market had generally approved the takeover but some worried NOL might not be able to achieve the necessary economies of scale needed for it to be successful.

Of the 30 STI component stocks, drinks firm Fraser & Neave fell 20 cents to Singapore $8.90 while food group Cerebos lost 30 cents to S$10.70. Multi-media firm Creative gained most, up S$1.10 to S$17.80 on rumours of a broker recommendation.
